claim: On host nativestack-5975wx-20260925 on 2026-10-01, the application-delivery recipe was qualified at Next.js 16.3.8 (tag v16.3.8, commit b0fad0d45eb4c4430fda5eeeb442e8a5af08a5f6, released 2026-09-30T16:13:46Z), whose release notes list seven security advisories, the most severe GHSA-cjq9-62q9-8jv4 (high: server-side request forgery in Image Optimization). The two-file patch (package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml, sha256 570ac44d237b6641a5087fe57b079aaf61dcb781b6496a721b0224dd17ea60d0) changes next, @next/env and the eight @next/swc-* lock entries, every other lock entry byte-identical. With Node v24.21.0 and pnpm 12.4.2 the frozen install, the peer check, the typecheck and the production build each exited 0 (recorded at 16:07:49Z), after a first frozen install at 12:13Z exited 1 with ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION for the ten packages published on 2026-09-30; no exclusion or policy change was made.
limitations: Bounded recipe checks only: make verify with its PostgreSQL, API and browser stages was not run, so the 2026-09-20 receipts still qualify 16.3.5, not 16.3.6 or 16.3.8.
The pnpm store, node_modules and build cache were warm from the earlier attempt; no cold-store install is claimed.
This recipe's exposure to the seven advisories was not established; the move removes the vulnerable versions from its lock.
Labels 15 to 17 are the version prints of Node and pnpm and a git diff check; they are metadata, not acceptance.
No new-host install ran: that is unit U10 on the new distribution. Provider usage of the builder is unknown.
